title: 1994 AHSME Problem 25
statement:
If \(x\) and \(y\) are non-zero real numbers such that

\[ |x|+y=3 \]

and

\[ |x|y+x^3=0, \] then the integer nearest to \(x-y\) is

solutions.text: If \(x\gt0,\) the second equation gives \(y=-x^2,\) while the first gives \(y=3-x;\) these would require \(x^2-x+3=0,\) which has no real root. Hence \(x\lt0.\) Put \(t=-x\gt0.\) Then the equations become \(t+y=3\) and \(ty-t^3=0,\) so \(y=t^2.\) Therefore \(x-y=-t-t^2=-3,\) already an integer. Thus the correct answer is A.
